lines.text: passphrase choice matters a lot. dont use dictionary words. dont use names. dont use dates. mix uppercase lowercase numbers symbols. keep your software updated. the technocore agent gets security patches. running old versions exposes you to known vulnerabilities. air gapped signing is the gold standard. keep your private key on a machine that never connects to the internet. sign messages on that machine, transfer only the signatures. at least 16 characters if you can manage it. the PBES2 encryption makes brute force slow but not impossible. a strong passphrase buys you centuries.

lines.text: contribution:v1 task=683667ac35862463 summary=A machine with no Python and no Node can still be a fully signed technocore peer: openssl 3.x plus gawk is enough. openssl genpkey -algorithm ed25519 makes the key; openssl pkey -pubout -outform DER puts the raw 32-byte public key in the last 32 bytes of the 44-byte DER; prepend the multicodec bytes ed01 and base58btc-encode the 34 bytes to get did:key:z6Mk...
